findings.sourceReading: Yamamoto has a strong inferiority complex toward Kinzo because Kinzo has more education than he does. His insecurity about being younger despite outranking Kinzo follows.
findings.alternative: Resentment may accompany that complex, and later hurt pride is retained, but a bit of a grudge substitutes a slight grievance for the explicitly strong sense of inferiority.

findings.description: Risk of losing transportability becomes transport already impossible.

contexts.japanesePS3: このままでは黄金が完全に輸送不能になってしまうことが明白となり、
contexts.WH: Now that it was clear that transporting the gold had become completely impossible, ......they had apparently decided on unloading it.
contexts.MG: Now that transporting the gold away had clearly become an impossible goal,
contexts.UP: It was clear that unless action was taken, the gold would soon become completely impossible to transport.

findings.sourceReading: If things continue as they are, the gold will become completely impossible to transport: the damaged submarine will sink, and the island cannot raise it. They apparently decide to unload the gold to avoid that outcome.
findings.alternative: Transporting the gold had become completely impossible removes このままでは and the prospective なってしまう. The preceding text establishes an inability to raise a sunken submarine, while the gold is currently being unloaded by winch. Later difficulty secretly shipping it off-island is a separate constraint.
